title: Germany's Economy Shows Tentative Signs of Life · 19 Aug
keywords: Germany, GDP growth, inflation, energy prices, industrial output, exports, China trade deficit, eurozone, purchasing power, economic recovery, Bundestag, European Central Bank, supply chain, trade dependence
notes: Germany posted modest growth in the second quarter of 2026, but a fresh rise in inflation and persistent vulnerabilities in its industrial trade model are undermining confidence in any durable rebound. Headline inflation climbed to 2.8 percent in July, erasing the relief many households had hoped to feel. The divergence between improving official data and the lived experience of citizens and firms is sharpening the political debate in Berlin.
